# 2 Baruch Chapter 19 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** First Fast and Vision

---

**19:1** "For though Adam was first to sin and brought untimely death upon all, yet those also who were born from him each one of them sinned for himself.

**19:2** Therefore each one of them was to himself both an Adam and an Eve.

**19:3** For in the case of Adam there was no compulsion on him, and still he sinned. And in the case of us also, there is no compulsion on us; and yet we also sin.

**19:4** Nevertheless Moses said to you: 'The commandment which I give you this day is not too difficult for you, nor is it far off.'

**19:5** But now, I say to you: The commandments of God are not too difficult for man; for if he have not sinned by willing his own evil, he can do that which is good.

**19:6** For just as there is no ground in the law for giving opportunity to evil, so there is no reason for excuse on account of the commandments.

**19:7** Yet even the reason for excuse was made certain beforehand for the righteous; for the law does not condemn the righteous in advance.

**19:8** For if a man walks in the ways of the Most High and does not sin out of the love of money, he shall not die before his time; for the Most High will not hold against any man more than what he has done in this world."

---

*SOPHIA notes: LOGOS base throughout. V.2 "both an Adam and an Eve" preserved as the striking theological formulation. V.4 Deut 30:11 quotation preserved formally. "Love of money" (v.8) preserved over PNEUMA's "greed" — the Syriac uses the specific mammon term, and "love of money" echoes 1 Tim 6:10.*
